is a set of rules and practices for how people exchange goods and services. There are four types of economic systems: traditional, command, market, and mixed. Read about one of these systems. Then answer the question below.
In a

, money was not widely used. Instead, people traded the goods and services they produced for other goods and services. Traditional economies were more common in small communities. For example, a hunter may have exchanged meat for crops grown by a neighbor. Or a farmer may have exchanged wheat for honey from a beekeeper. Economic activity was guided by traditions, so people often did the same kind of work as previous generations, using the same methods.

textContent.text: One challenge of traditional economies was that people didn't often need the exact same amounts of the goods or services they traded. Also, it could be difficult to know how much one good or service was worth when compared directly to other goods and services. So, traditional economies are not very common in the present day. Using money is more common because it simplifies trade.
